desc:
In one move you may pick one element of nums and increase or decrease it by exactly 1. Return the minimum number of moves needed to make all elements equal.

For example, [1, 2, 3] needs 2 moves (change 1 to 2 and 3 to 2), and [4, 10, 1, 1] needs 12.
hints: Each element must travel to a common target t; element x costs |x - t|.
You want to minimize the sum of absolute distances to one point. Moving the target one step to the right helps the elements on the right and hurts those on the left.
The sum of absolute deviations is minimized at the median. Sort the array and sum the distances to nums[n // 2].
editorial: Let f(t) = sum |x - t|. When t moves one step right, every element to its left gets one step farther and every element to its right gets one step closer. So f decreases as long as more than half of the elements are to the right of t, and it increases once more than half are to the left. The minimum is therefore reached at a median.

Sort the array, take the middle element (either of the two middle ones when n is even, the sum is the same) and add up the absolute differences. Sorting dominates at O(n log n). Quickselect finds the median in O(n) average time. Another way to see the same sum: pair the smallest with the largest element; each pair (lo, hi) costs exactly hi - lo moves regardless of the target between them.
